A capabilities report with nothing after the <: it lists no capabilities, so it is malformed.
A capabilities report of empty items: once they are dropped it lists nothing, so it is malformed.
An NMEA time with a fraction of a second ending in zero: the neutral form drops the trailing zero.
A status that is only a 6-character locator, with no symbol after it, is plain status text: the locator form needs its symbol (APRS12c ch. 16).
An Agrelo DFjr bearing report: bearing and quality.
A control character in a token (0x1C here) makes the report free text (free-text-capabilities, tolerated).
A control character in a value (0x1C here) makes the report free text, as one in a token does (free-text-capabilities, tolerated).
=43 has a value but no token, so it is neither TOKEN nor TOKEN=VALUE: free text (free-text-capabilities, tolerated).
Spaces around an item, and around its =, are padding: the token is MSG_CNT and the value 43.
Only spaces are trimmed from an item: a CR left at the end of a token is a control character, so the report is free text (free-text-capabilities, tolerated).
U+00A0 is neither a space nor a control character, so it does not make a token free text.
One capability is valid UTF-8 and the next is not: the whole text is read as Latin-1, not each item on its own (non-utf8-text, tolerated).
A general query type is upper-case letters; IGAT7 is not one (invalid-general-query).
The footprint radius is a fixed 4-digit number (APRS12c ch. 15); 020 is not (invalid-general-query).
A footprint latitude of 100.02 degrees is not a latitude (invalid-general-query).
^B7 is lifted from the end of the status text; the space before it is text as sent.
With a locator, the one space before the text is dropped, and the space before ^B7 is kept.
0 is not an ERP code (they run 1 to K, APRS12c ch. 16), so ^B0 is status text, not a beam heading.
APRS12c ch. 19 places no restriction on user-defined data, header included, so a control byte as the packet type is written back as it came.
The source in a third-party header may be 1-9 printable ASCII characters other than > and : (APRS12c ch. 17), so PY2SP_R-R is a source, though it would not be one in an APRS-IS header.
A path entry in a third-party header is an address, 1-9 letters, digits or -; TC+IP is not (invalid-third-party).
A third-party packet whose inner information field is empty re-encodes with that field as received: empty.
The Agrelo format is %, 3 bearing digits, / and 1 quality digit; a second quality digit is not part of it (invalid-agrelo-df).
A bearing of 361 degrees is not a bearing (invalid-agrelo-df).
Text after $ that has no NMEA address field is not an NMEA sentence: invalid-nmea, an error in both modes.
Seven characters after $ with no comma: not an NMEA sentence.
An address field with no comma and no fields after it is not a sentence.
A six-character address that does not start with P is not an NMEA address field, so the sentence is not read as RMC.
A four-character address and a wrong checksum: the address is read first, so the error is invalid-nmea.
A proprietary sentence (P, a manufacturer code, more characters) is NMEA and is kept as text.
A user-configured talker ID (U1) is a valid address; the sentence is read as GGA.
A DEL byte in a sentence: not printable ASCII, so invalid-nmea.
A latitude whose minutes are 60 or more is not a coordinate; the position is left out and the rest of the sentence is read.
A latitude with only two digits before the point has no degrees; it is not read as 0 degrees.
A latitude of 91 degrees is out of range; the position is left out.
A latitude with an empty longitude is no position at all.
Hour 25 is not a time; the time is left out and the rest is read.
Seven digits are not hhmmss (and nor are five): the time is left out, not read from the first six.
Five digits and a fraction are not hhmmss; the time is left out.
A GLL status that is neither A nor V says nothing about the fix.
GGA's quality indicator is one digit; 05 is not one, so the fix is left out.
A sentence that stops early: the fields that are there are read.
A VTG with only its course: the course is read.
Garmin's PGRMC ends in RMC but is proprietary, so none of its fields are read.
TinyTrack's comment after a sentence's checksum: the sentence ends at the checksum, which is checked, and the rest is the comment.
TinyTrack's comment after a checksum that does not match: the sentence ends at its checksum, which is checked, so the corruption is caught.
A * not followed by two hex digits is a reserved character in a field, not a checksum: invalid-nmea.
A time fraction is kept exactly as sent: .429 is 23:03:18.429, not a floating-point neighbour of it.
Every digit of a long time fraction is kept, not cut at a fixed precision.

The inner header marks two path entries used (multiple-used-markers): lenient decoding reads it, with the warning on the inner packet; strict gives invalid-third-party; and it is not re-encoded, since the inner packet's diagnostics are part of the data.
P and three characters is a proprietary address: the sentence is NMEA, kept as text, not read as GLL.
A proprietary sentence with a checksum that does not match: the structure is valid, so the error is the checksum.

An empty destination inside a third-party header is a tolerated defect of the inner header: decoded with its warning on the inner packet, which is written with destination "" as any header is; strict rejects it, and an encoder refuses it.
An NMEA number may start with its decimal point: .30 is a speed of 0.3 knots.
A q-construct is read only in the outer header. In a third-party header, qAR and the station after it are path entries like any other, and the inner packet has no q_construct.
Only a positive footprint value may have a leading space; - 17.15 has a space after its minus sign, so it is not a number: invalid-general-query.
APRS12c: "Note the leading space in the latitude, as its value is positive". The space marks a positive value, so a space before -34.02 is not a number: invalid-general-query.
A footprint value is a number as a telemetry value is: an optional minus sign, then digits with an optional decimal point and at least one digit, so -.1715 is a longitude.
